source: RFC 0014 R4 (the maintainer's answer of 2026-11-24: reserve them; the rules hard, the policies flexible); RFC 0005 §5 (sentences proposed in the PR)
statement: The characters a future pattern syntax needs, `[ ] ( ) | ! ^ $ \`, are a compile error unescaped in every pattern of a document and of a route map: an http:path: pattern, a typed resource pattern (its type and literal segments), an action pattern (its service and verb), a route's path and the literal segments of its resource template; the error names the character, printably (a control character as its \uXXXX escape), and its position. A backslash followed by one of `[ ] ( ) | ! ^ $ \ * ? { }` is that character as text, and followed by anything else is a compile error, so every literal has one spelling and an escaped character never acts as syntax. A path pattern that matches no request path does not compile either: a backslash (PIP-14), a `;` or a control character (PIP-5, PIP-30), a dot segment (PIP-5), or a segment whose values hold more than 256 characters. An escape counts as the one character it writes in a pattern's length. cosec-migrate escapes a 7.x path pattern's reserved characters, which 7.x read as text, and cosec-openapi escapes every metacharacter of a spec path outside its templates.
